title: Universal electrical resistivity in iron-based high-temperature superconductors
abstract: arXiv:2610.23865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity $\rho(T)$ in cuprate, iron-based, and nickelate superconductors represents one of unresolved problems in modern solid-state physics, because of the high absolute value of $\rho(T)$, which, in many cases, exceeds the Ioffe-Rigel criterion, and a large difference in the $\rho(T)$ shape for samples with different doping. Here I show that the nearest neighbors parallel resistivity model (arXiv: 2607.23484) can well describe the in-plane resistivity $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in iron-based superconductors (IBS) of type 11, 111, 122, 1111, 1144 and 42214 in which the spin density wave phase or nematic order is suppressed by doping. The model is based on the postulate that $\rho_{ab}(T)$ is a sum of two parallel conduction channels, where one channel is described by the Bloch-Gr\"uneisen equation and the other by the Arrhenius hopping equation. Consequently, the variety of $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in the IBS is explained as a variation of the Debye temperature $\Theta_D$ and the hopping activation energy $E_a$. The derived Debye temperatures were used to estimate the electron-phonon coupling constant $\lambda_{e-ph}$in the studied IBS.
summary:
- Shows that IBS in‑plane resistivity follows a parallel‑channel model (Bloch‑Grüneisen + Arrhenius hopping).
- Attributes the varied ρ(T) shapes across 11, 111, 122, 1111, 1144, 42214 families to changes in Θ_D and E_a.
- Uses derived Θ_D to estimate electron‑phonon coupling λₑ₋ph, linking resistivity to superconducting pairing.

title: Multiple propagating modes in random polycrystals
authors: Ming Huang, Stanislav I. Rokhlin, Michael J. S. Lowe
abstract: arXiv:2610.24047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiple-scattering theory predicts that the coherent elastic wave in a statistically isotropic polycrystal is not a single wave. Its dispersion equation admits multiple roots of a given polarization, but these extra modes have never been observed. Here, using grain-scale finite-element simulations of three-dimensional polycrystals, we resolve the coherent field in the frequency--wavenumber plane and directly observe the predicted multiplicity for both transverse and longitudinal excitations: a single mode at low frequencies gives way to two in the geometric regime as the wavelength approaches the grain correlation length. The measured modes follow the roots of the dispersion equation, which always carries a third root whose attenuation exceeds that of the others. It is this attenuation hierarchy, not the root count, that dictates how many modes propagate and can be observed. Coherent wave propagation in random media is thus inherently multimodal in the geometric regime, which we reach here for the first time in polycrystals.
summary:
- Finite‑element simulations show coherent elastic waves in isotropic polycrystals split into multiple propagating modes.
- When the wavelength nears the grain size, a single low‑frequency mode bifurcates into two observable modes for both transverse and longitudinal excitations, matching dispersion‑equation roots.
- The third theoretical root has much higher attenuation; attenuation hierarchy, not root count, dictates which modes actually propagate.

title: Two quantum spin liquid states coexisting in the kagome antiferromagnet herbertsmithite
authors: Arthur C. Campello, Shengtao Jiang, Wei He, Jiajia Wen, Daniel M. Pajerowski, Steven A. Kivelson, Hong-Chen Jiang, Young S. Lee
abstract: arXiv:2610.24065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Herbertsmithite (ZnCu$_3$(OH)$_6$Cl$_2$) is one of the most extensively studied quantum spin liquid (QSL) candidates, yet the precise nature of its ground state remains unresolved. Here, we compare the results of high-resolution inelastic neutron scattering on single crystals of herbertsmithite (Zn$_\mathrm{x}$Cu$_\mathrm{4-x}$(OD)$_6$Cl$_2$, $x\simeq 0.85$) with large-scale density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and dynamical DMRG simulations to benchmark the spin Hamiltonian and uncover fundamental properties of the ground state. The measured spin correlations determine an energy density for the Heisenberg model that closely matches simulations, an essential verification of the Hamiltonian. In parallel, DMRG simulations reveal two nearly degenerate QSL states. Both preserve translational symmetry, but one retains the lattice point-group symmetries whereas the other develops anisotropic spin correlations that break point-group symmetry. These two QSLs have distinct spin structure factors, and, remarkably, close agreement with the neutron spectra is achieved with an admixture of the two states. Our results establish a quantitative correspondence between neutron scattering and simulations, and suggest that herbertsmithite realizes a regime in which two proximate gapped QSL states coexist.
summary:
- Neutron scattering on ZnCu₃(OH)₆Cl₂ matches the Heisenberg model energy density, confirming the Hamiltonian.
- DMRG reveals two nearly degenerate gapped QSLs: one preserving point‑group symmetry, the other breaking it with anisotropic correlations.
- Experimental spectra are best reproduced by a mixture of the two QSLs

title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
authors: Hyungkun Bong, Choongjae Won, Seongyong Lee, Soomin Oh, Phuong X. Nguyen, Raghav Chaturvedi, Sehyun Oh, Jiyong Han, Paul Malinowski, Chad Mowers, Jimin Kim, Sae Hee Ryu, Hyunjong Lee, Jinhyeok Choi, Sangsu Yer, Chris Jozwiak, Aaron Bostwick, Eli Rotenberg, Craig M. Polley, Matthew D. Watson, Timur K. Kim, Heejun Yang, Jieun Lee, Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan, Jae-Hoon Park, Gil Young Cho, Kyle M. Shen, Mingu Kang
abstract: arXiv:2610.24071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kagome lattice materials host a remarkably rich landscape of novel quantum phenomena, all arising from the intrinsic interplay of topology, correlation, and frustration. While previous studies have been mostly limited to bulk three-dimensional (3D) kagome crystals, the realization of a true two-dimensional (2D) kagome system has remained a long-standing goal, to unlock fundamentally new physics and engineering pathways inaccessible in 3D systems. In this work, we establish the first ideal 2D monolayer kagome lattices by leveraging a novel and versatile van der Waals (vdW) kagome family, A2T3X4 (A = K, Rb, Cs; T = Ni, Pd, Pt; X = S, Se). Our nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) directly characterizes the electronic structure of A2T3X4 down to the monolayer limit, notably revealing an isolated kagome-derived flat band just below the Fermi level. Via gate-engineering of 2D A2T3X4, the kagome flat band can be further tuned to the Fermi level, allowing direct access to the partially filled flat band physics and establishing a qualitatively new 2D flat band platform. Compared to existing moire-based artificial flat band systems, this vdW kagome-based intrinsic flat band system realizes more than 220 times higher flat band electron density, opening an entirely new density and energy regime for exploring 2D flat band physics. Harnessing this high-electron-density flat band in 2D vdW kagome system provides a clear pathway to scale emergent flat band phenomena - such as fractional quantum anomalous Hall states - to far higher temperatures than currently achievable, as long-envisioned in theory and further supported by our many-body calculations.
summary:
- First true 2D monolayer kagome lattice (A₂T₃X₄) with an isolated flat band just below the Fermi level.
- Nano‑ARPES confirms the flat band; gate tuning can bring it to the Fermi level for partially filled flat‑band physics.
- Achieves >220× the flat‑band electron density of moiré systems, opening a new high‑density 2D flat‑band regime.

title: Quantifying the Kinetic and Thermodynamic Origins of the Glass-Forming Ability in Metals
authors: Weiwei Jin, Jinpeng Fan, Mark D. Shattuck, Corey S. O'Hern
abstract: arXiv:2610.24101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The glass-forming ability (GFA) of a metallic liquid can be quantified by the critical cooling rate $R_c$, below which it crystallizes upon cooling. $R_c$ is determined by the competition between $R$ and the crystallization rate $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$. Here, we calculate $R_c$ and $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$ in model pure metals and alloys with BCC/B2 and FCC equilibrium crystal structures. Using classical nucleation theory and independently calculated crystal growth rates, we evaluate $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}=(IU^3)^{1/4}$ at $T=0.8T_m$, where $I$ and $U$ are the nucleation and growth rates and $T_m$ is the melting temperature. We find a strong positive correlation between $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$ and $R_c$ over eleven orders of magnitude. We decompose $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$ into a product of a kinetic contribution, involving atomic cluster attachment and diffusion, and a thermodynamic contribution. We show that the thermodynamic contribution to $\mathcal{K}_{\rm X}$ dominates the kinetic contribution over the range of cooling rates that we consider. The nucleation barrier $\Delta G_c \sim \tilde\gamma^3/\Delta\tilde\mu^2$, where $\tilde\gamma$ is the reduced effective liquid--crystal interfacial free energy and $\Delta\tilde\mu$ is the reduced bulk driving force, determines the magnitude of the thermodynamic contribution. The relative importance of $\tilde\gamma$ and $\Delta\tilde\mu$ depends on the material: a large interfacial free energy can suppress nucleation in some systems, whereas a weak bulk driving force can inhibit crystallization in others. Analyses of the structural and chemical order show that better glass formers have enhanced structural frustration, more icosahedral-like and less crystal-like local environments, and a larger chemical-order mismatch between the supercooled liquid and crystal phases.
summary:
- GFA measured by critical cooling rate \(R_c\), strongly correlated with crystallization rate \(\mathcal{K}_X\).
- \(\mathcal{K}_X=(IU^^{1/4}\) splits into kinetic (attachment/diffusion) and thermodynamic (nucleation barrier) terms; thermodynamics dominates.
- Nucleation barrier \(\Delta G_c \sim \tilde\gamma^3/\Delta\tilde\mu^2\); the balance of interfacial energy \(\tilde\gamma\) and driving force \(\Delta\tilde\mu\) varies across materials.

title: Gate-defined quantum dot and charge noise analysis in a Forksheet transistor
authors: Dominic Leclerc, Claude Rohrbacher, Alexis Morel, Joffrey Rivard, Romain Ritzenthaler, Christian Lupien, Hans Mertens, Naoto Horiguchi, Eva Dupont-Ferrier
abstract: arXiv:2610.24136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the cryogenic characterization of a 14-nm nMOS Forksheet transistor down to 10 mK. We demonstrate that the device retains transistor operation with improved characteristics at cryogenic temperatures, while also forming a gate-defined quantum dot that can be tuned to the single-electron regime. In the quantum-dot regime, we perform low-frequency charge-noise measurements across different charge occupations and observe an average charge-noise amplitude of $\langle S_0\rangle = 10\;\mu\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ at 1 Hz, with a minimum measured value of $3.3\;\mu\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$. These results highlight the potential of Forksheet technology for the monolithic cointegration of quantum and classical CMOS functionalities in future quantum processors.
summary:
- Cryogenic 14‑nm nMOS Forksheet transistor operates at 10 mK with improved characteristics.
- Gate defines a quantum dot tunable to the single‑electron regime.
- Charge‑noise amplitude: ⟨S₀⟩ = 10 µeV/√Hz at 1 Hz, minimum 3 µeV/√Hz.

title: Boundary Element Modeling for THz-SNOM Near-Field Probes
authors: Noah Reich, Richard Kim, Thomas Koschny, Jigang Wang
abstract: arXiv:2610.24151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Terahertz scanning near-field optical microscopy (THz-SNOM) enables spatially and spectrally resolved investigation of low-energy collective and topological states in quantum materials and nano-structured devices by exploiting the strongly localized near field generated by a polarized atomic force microscopy (AFM) tip. Because the THz near-field response is highly sensitive to tip geometry, understanding how geometric parameters control field confinement and decay is essential for selecting tip designs that provide the spatial resolution required for specific experiments. In this work, we develop a boundary element method (BEM) for modeling the electrostatic near-field of a conducting AFM tip in response to an external background field. The tip is represented by a simplified closed, blunt-cone geometry with its surface discretized into panels using increased mesh density near the apex. A modified Green's function is used to calculate interactions between surface panels, while an augmented linear system simultaneously enforces the equipotential boundary condition on the conducting surface and overall charge neutrality to determine the induced surface-charge distribution. We validate the BEM by comparing the resulting near-field decay with that obtained from a three-dimensional quasi-static COMSOL Multiphysics simulation. The BEM accurately reproduces the COMSOL field-decay behavior while requiring orders of magnitude fewer mesh elements and substantially reducing computational cost. These results demonstrate that the BEM provides an accurate and computationally efficient framework for systematically investigating the dependence of THz near-field confinement on AFM tip geometry. This framework can be extended to more complex and experimentally realistic tip geometries, providing a route toward rational tip selection and design for application-specific spatial-resolution requirements.
summary:
- Developed a boundary element method (BEM) to model electrostatic near‑field of a blunt‑cone AFM tip for THz‑SNOM.
- Used a modified Green’s function and augmented linear system to enforce equipotentiality and charge neutrality, enabling efficient surface‑charge distribution calculation.
- Validated BEM against 3‑D COMSOL simulations, achieving accurate field‑decay predictions with far fewer mesh elements.

title: Kohler's Rule Holds in the Strange Metallic Hubbard Model
authors: Rebekah M. Jin, Emily Z. Zhang, Jixun K. Ding, Brian Moritz, Thomas P. Devereaux
abstract: arXiv:2610.24208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unconventional magnetotransport violating Kohler's rule has been reported in many strongly correlated strange metals, but the exact origin of these violations is yet unknown. To investigate this question, we use determinant quantum Monte Carlo to compute the magnetoresistance of the hole-doped Hubbard-Hofstadter model. Despite $T$-linear resistivity exceeding the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit and the nominal absence of well-defined quasiparticles, we find Kohler's rule unexpectedly holds across a wide range of on-site interaction strengths and hole dopings. In particular, Kohler emerges below a crossover temperature $T^\star\approx t$ identified from the double occupancy and specific heat, coinciding with the onset of local singlet correlations between lattice sites. We thus propose that Kohler scaling in this regime reflects a more general form of many-body quantum coherence. Our results show that strong correlations and strange metallicity do not themselves generically produce anomalous magnetoresistance.
summary:
- Kohler’s rule surprisingly holds in the hole‑doped Hubbard‑Hofstadter model despite T‑linear resistivity and lack of quasiparticles.
- The rule emerges below a crossover temperature \(T^\star \approx t\), marked by local singlet formation and changes in double occupancy and specific heat.
- Findings suggest that strong correlations and strange metallicity alone do not cause anomalous magnetoresistance; Kohler scaling reflects a broader many‑body quantum coherence.

title: Role of chirality in the polarizer-filter dichotomy in nonmagnetic junctions
abstract: arXiv:2610.24226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chirality-induced spin selectivity can enable spin generation by nonmagnetic junctions, but its symmetry requirements remain debated. We show that the symmetry of the junction constrains its polarizing behavior: a spin polarizer requires a chiral junction, whereas an achiral junction can act as a spin filter. This symmetry involves the junction as a whole, not only the molecule. Achiral molecules can act as polarizers or filters depending on junction geometry, as confirmed with a minimal tight-binding model. Reciprocity forbids polarization detection by linear two-terminal magnetoresistance; we propose a nonlocal measurement that distinguishes polarizers from filters and establishes whether the junction breaks time-reversal symmetry.
summary:
- Spin polarizers need chiral junctions; achiral junctions act as spin filters.
- Junction symmetry—not just molecular chirality—determines polarizing behavior; geometry can toggle achiral molecules between polarizer and filter.
- Linear two‑terminal MR cannot detect polarization; a nonlocal measurement distinguishes polarizers from filters and probes time‑reversal symmetry breaking.

title: Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A$_2$T$_3$X$_4$
authors: Soomin Oh, Jiyong Han, Jinhyeok Choi, Donghae Seo, Mingu Kang, Gil Young Cho
abstract: arXiv:2610.24633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moir\'e materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the recently synthesized van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.
summary:
- Monolayer A₂T₃X₄ kagome sheets provide intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions, enabling high‑temperature fractional Chern insulators.
- Exact diagonalization reveals ferromagnetism over wide fillings, producing fractional Chern insulators, composite Fermi liquids, and charge‑ordered states; Cs₂Pd₃S₄ shows a ~26 meV many‑body gap.
- Bilayer stacks with antiparallel magnetizations support fractional quantum spin Hall insulators at realistic interlayer separations.

title: Microwave probing of magnetic phases in a dipolar-exchange magnet LiGdF$_4$
authors: S. S. Sosin, A. I. Smirnov, T. A. Soldatov, V. S. Edelman, O. A. Morozov, S. L. Korableva, I. V. Romanova
abstract: arXiv:2610.24734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the results of low-temperature magnetic resonance measurements performed on a single-crystal sample of a weakly anisotropic dipolar-exchange antiferromagnet LiGdF$_4$. The transformation of a resonance spectrum due to the formation of the ordered phase is observed at temperatures below $T_N=0.19(1)$ K. A sequence of field-induced phase transitions is detected for the external magnetic field applied along the fourfold axis of the crystal. A well-resolved magnetic resonance spectrum is observed in one of the low-field magnetic phases as well as above the saturation field. Competing exchange and dipolar interactions, as a special type of magnetic frustration, are suggested to account for the delayed ordering and complex magnetic phase diagram of the system.
summary:
- Low‑temperature magnetic resonance on LiGdF₄ shows a resonance spectrum change below T_N = 19 K, indicating magnetic ordering.
- Field‑induced phase transitions appear for H∥[001], with a distinct low‑field phase exhibiting a well‑resolved resonance spectrum.
- Competing dipolar and exchange interactions create magnetic frustration, explaining delayed ordering and the complex phase diagram.

title: Interaction-driven competing instabilities in two-dimensional checkerboard quadratic band crossing semimetals
authors: Jia-Hao Wen, Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang
abstract: arXiv:2610.25046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional quadratic band crossing point (QBCP) semimetals serve as a fertile platform for interaction-driven quantum criticality, nevertheless, the role of the complete fermion-fermion interactions remains largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically investigate the low-energy physics of a spin-1/2 checkerboard-lattice QBCP semimetal by considering all 16 marginally short-range fermion-fermion interactions. Using the momentum-shell renormalization group, we derive the coupled flow equations, which reveal that the low-energy physics is governed by a series of fixed points. Depending on the initial conditions, the system may exhibit a single stable fixed point, several discrete fixed points, or three continuous groups of fixed points parameterized by a few variables. By introducing source terms and evaluating susceptibilities, we identify the dominant and subdominant instabilities. The leading phases include nematic spin-nematic (NSN), quantum anomalous Hall (QAH), chiral superconducting ($\mathrm{SC}_1$), and quantum spin Hall (QSH) orders. Moreover, several features distinguish our findings from previous simplified models. Off-diagonal interactions generate terms that promote orders absent in such models, the continuous groups allow systematic tuning of the leading instability, and trajectory-dependent instabilities emerge where the full RG flow, rather than the fixed point alone, determines the dominant state. These results offer a comprehensive theoretical understanding of low-energy quantum critical behaviors and phase instabilities in two-dimensional QBCP semimetals and related electron systems.
summary:
- Analyzed all 16 marginal short‑range interactions in a 2D checkerboard QBCP semimetal using momentum‑shell RG, uncovering single, discrete, and continuous fixed‑point families.
- Determined dominant instabilities—nematic spin‑nematic, quantum anomalous Hall, chiral superconductivity, and quantum spin Hall—whose hierarchy depends on RG trajectories.
- Showed off‑diagonal interactions generate new orders, continuous fixed‑point groups allow systematic tuning of the leading phase, and full RG flow, not just fixed points, dictates the final state.

title: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions and deconfined criticality in SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$
abstract: arXiv:2610.25081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$ is the leading candidate for deconfined criticality, yet theories of its critical regime omit the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions, which gap the kagome Dirac spin liquid. Adding them to the SU(2) gauge theory, we show that time reversal and a spin-orbit-locked glide forbid any gauge-singlet spinon mass to all orders. In-plane DM only twists the spinons, reconstructing the nodes below $0.03$-$0.17$ K, while out-of-plane DM is irrelevant and SO(5) anisotropy arises only at second order. The material thus remains a platform for deconfined criticality, which NMR can test, since a $[100]$ field induces a N\'eel moment and a $[001]$ field does not.
summary:
- DM terms preserve deconfined criticality; symmetry forbids spinon mass.
- In‑plane DM twists spinons, moving Dirac nodes

title: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions in the SU(2) gauge theory of the Shastry-Sutherland Dirac spin liquids
abstract: arXiv:2610.25082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the fermion bilinears of the SU(2) gauge theory of the Shastry-Sutherland Dirac spin liquids under the spin-orbit-locked space group and treat the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions of SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$ at leading order in $1/N$ and at one loop. At linear order DM can neither gap the spinons nor destabilize the SO(5) point above a scale $T^*$. Symmetry forbids every local gauge-singlet fermion mass at any order. Among the singlet bilinears, the in-plane couplings induce only a conserved spin current of dimension exactly 2, which sets $T^*=4\lambda\simeq0.03$-$0.17$ K, and the out-of-plane coupling only a flavored spin-2 current, irrelevant at a unitary critical point. DM-induced Yukawa couplings start below $2\%$ of the one that bounds the pseudocritical window. In zero field, measured samples order above $1$ K, at or above $T^*$. Below $T^*$, in a two-dimensional sample at the critical pressure, the Dirac cones reconstruct into a chirally protected $d$-wave quadratic band touching whose only gauge-singlet gap channels are the two valence-bond components and the scalar chirality. A one-loop flow, with the gauge field screened by the band touching, ends at $T^{**}\sim(0.03$-$0.1)\lambda$ on a ray containing valence-bond order for the material's exchange and for most random couplings, and otherwise on a gapped chiral $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquid. The DM bias between the two plaquette patterns is at most of order $10^{-4}$, with a direction not fixed at $O(1/N)$, whereas non-magnetic quenched disorder couples a relevant random field to the plaquette doublet and none to the chirality. A field along $[100]$ induces a $(\pi,\pi)$ N\'eel moment linear in the field; a field along $[001]$ does not. This selection rule also holds in the dimer phase and is testable by $^{11}$B NMR under pressure.
summary:
- Classified SU(gauge‑theory fermion bilinears for Shastry–Sutherland Dirac spin liquids under spin–orbit‑locked space group; treated DM interactions at leading \(1/N\) and one‑loop order.
- Linear DM terms cannot gap spinons or destabilize the SO(point; they generate only conserved spin currents, fixing a crossover scale \(T^*\approx03\!-\!17\)

title: Large exchange bias from coupled antiferromagnetic order and glassy magnetic freezing in $Co_{0.36}NbS_{2}$
authors: Suman Mondal (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, Israel), Himadri Roy Dakua (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, Israel), Raz Luger (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, Israel), Muntaser Naamneh (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, Israel), Eran Maniv (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, Israel)
abstract: arXiv:2610.25102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetization measurements on single-crystalline $Co_{0.36}NbS_{2}$ reveal antiferromagnetic order near $T_{N} \simeq 26 K$ and a lower-temperature history-dependent magnetic response consistent with glassy freezing of a subset of magnetic moments. After field cooling, $M(H)$ loops exhibit a sizable exchange-bias shift, reaching $|H_{EB}| \simeq 4.4 kOe$ at $1.8 K$ for a $70 kOe$ field-cooling sweep protocol. The training effect, field-sweep and cooling-field protocol dependence, and disappearance of the bias near a blocking temperature $T_{B} \simeq 12 K$, well below $T_{N}$, support an interpretation in which frozen uncompensated moments are exchange-coupled to an antiferromagnetic matrix. These results suggest that antiferromagnetic-glassy-moment coupling may provide a broader route to exchange bias in off-stoichiometric magnetic $NbS_{2}$ intercalates.
summary:
- Co₀.₃₆NbS₂ orders antiferromagnetically at TN ≈ 26 K and exhibits glassy freezing of a subset of moments below TB ≈ 12 K.
- Field‑cooling produces a large exchange‑bias shift (|HEB| ≈ 4 kOe at 8 K) that disappears above TB.
- The bias shows training, sweep‑field, and cooling‑field dependence, indicating coupling of frozen uncompensated moments to the antiferromagnetic matrix.

title: Frustration-Assisted Electrical Switching in $Co_xTaS_2$
authors: Matan Sterenberg (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, Israel), Bar Segura (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, Israel), Muntaser Naamneh (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, Israel), Eran Maniv (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, Israel)
abstract: arXiv:2610.25112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrical switching in antiferromagnets is commonly described as the action of current-induced torques on a rigid order parameter. In frustrated magnets, however, competing states can create a history-dependent energy landscape in which slow collective dynamics actively participate in electrical reconfiguration. Here, we demonstrate frustration-assisted switching in near-stoichiometric $Co_xTaS_2$, a van der Waals antiferromagnet located at the composition-sensitive boundary between Hall-active and Hall-inactive multi-Q-related magnetic regimes. Although the crystals exhibit no resolved spontaneous Hall response, they retain van Hove singularities near the Fermi level and order antiferromagnetically below $T_N \simeq 31.5 K$. Current pulses write nonvolatile anisotropic resistance states in microstructured devices, with an activation current density nearly an order of magnitude below that reported for the Hall-active lower-intercalation phase. The switching response separates into two temperature-dependent dynamical regimes rather than following a single current threshold. Independent magnetization-aging and post-field-relaxation measurements reveal slow, history-dependent magnetic dynamics, and the relaxation strength closely follows the inverse switching amplitude. These results identify magnetic frustration and glassy dynamics as central ingredients in the electrical reconfiguration of $Co_xTaS_2$, establishing a route to functional switching through a dynamically soft antiferromagnetic landscape.
summary:
- Demonstrated nonvolatile anisotropic resistance switching in near‑stoichiometric CoₓTaS₂ driven by current pulses, with activation current density ~10× lower than Hall‑active phase.
- Identified two distinct temperature‑dependent dynamical regimes and slow, history‑dependent magnetic relaxation linked to frustration‑induced glassy dynamics.
- Established magnetic frustration and collective glassy behavior as key mechanisms enabling efficient electrical reconfiguration in this van der Waals antiferromagnet.
